record.context_brief: uniform finite-versus-infinite behavior of Betti-number suprema
record.original_question: Fix an embedding dimension e and let F be a family of numerical semigroups with that fixed embedding dimension. For each i = 1, ..., e - 1 define B_i(F) = sup{ b_i(R_Gamma) | Gamma in F }, where R_Gamma is the local semigroup ring of Gamma. Must it be true that the quantities B_i(F) are either all finite or all infinite?

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Let F be a family of numerical semigroups with fixed embedding dimension e. Define Bi(F) = sup{ bi(RΓ ) | Γ ∈ F } for i = 1,...,e − 1. Is it true that the Bi(F) are either all finite or all infinite?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be a numerical semigroup, that is, a cofinite submonoid of $(\mathbb{N},+)$ containing $0$. Let $e(\Gamma)$ denote its embedding dimension (the cardinality of its minimal system of generators). For a field $k$, let $R_\Gamma = k[[t^\gamma : \gamma \in \Gamma]]$ be the associated one-dimensional local semigroup ring, and let $b_i(R_\Gamma) = \dim_k \mathrm{Tor}_i^{R_\Gamma}(k,k)$ denote the $i$-th Betti number of $R_\Gamma$ (which is a Cohen–Macaulay local ring of embedding dimension $e(\Gamma)$, so $b_i(R_\Gamma)$ is nonzero precisely for $i=0,1,\dots,e(\Gamma)-1$).

Fix an integer $e \ge 2$ and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of numerical semigroups all of embedding dimension $e$. For $i = 1, \dots, e-1$ define
$$B_i(\mathcal{F}) = \sup\{\, b_i(R_\Gamma) : \Gamma \in \mathcal{F}\,\} \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}.$$

Is it true that for every such family $\mathcal{F}$, the values $B_1(\mathcal{F}), B_2(\mathcal{F}), \dots, B_{e-1}(\mathcal{F})$ are either all finite or all infinite?
artifact.category_tag: Betti numbers of numerical semigroup rings
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about uniform finite-vs-infinite behavior of the Betti number suprema $B_i(\mathcal{F})$ over families of numerical semigroups with fixed embedding dimension $e$. While it is classical (Bresinsky and successors) that for $e \ge 4$ the individual Betti numbers can be unbounded over all numerical semigroups of embedding dimension $e$, no source found in a web search resolves the dichotomy question (all-finite vs all-infinite) for arbitrary subfamilies $\mathcal{F}$. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Unboundedness of Betti Numbers of Curves
status_evidence.snippet: Bresinsky constructed a class of monomial curves in A^4 to prove that β1(4) = ∞, using this to prove β1(r) = ∞ for every r ≥ 4.
status_evidence.claim: Individual Betti numbers can be unbounded across all numerical semigroups of a fixed embedding dimension e ≥ 4, motivating the dichotomy question but not resolving it for arbitrary subfamilies.

status_evidence.title: Betti numbers for numerical semigroup rings
status_evidence.snippet: Survey results related to the magnitude of the Betti numbers of numerical semigroup rings and of their tangent cones.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys on Betti numbers of numerical semigroup rings discuss boundedness phenomena but do not establish the proposed all-finite-or-all-infinite dichotomy.
